# MEANTIME attribution

## What is attributed here

The 30 operational TextGraphs were generated by TextGraphX from the raw Wikinews articles and retained source-file metadata. No manual MEANTIME annotations were used to generate the TextGraphs or evaluate semantic projection in this study.

The original MEANTIME CC BY 4.0 licence file was retrieved from the annotated dataset archive and preserved unchanged in third_party/MEANTIME/LICENSE.txt. The annotated files are not redistributed. MEANTIME attribution applies to retained corpus-packaging metadata, while the source-bearing operational TextGraphs derive from Wikinews articles distributed under CC BY 2.5.

## What is not claimed

The present semantic-projection experiment does not use MEANTIME manual
annotations. The operational TextGraphs were not copied from the annotated
MEANTIME files. Earlier published TextGraphX evaluation did use MEANTIME
manual annotations. That evaluation is not repeated in this study.

## Corpus citation

Minard, Anne-Lyse, Manuela Speranza, Ruben Urizar, Begoña Altuna, Marieke van
Erp, Anneleen Schoen, and Chantal van Son. 2016. MEANTIME, the NewsReader
Multilingual Event and Time Corpus. In Proceedings of the Tenth International
Conference on Language Resources and Evaluation (LREC 2016). European Language
Resources Association.

The bibliographic record is `CORPUS_CITATION.bib`.

## Licence

The Wikinews article text in the operational graphs is CC BY 2.5. MEANTIME packaging metadata is attributed under CC BY 4.0. The annotated MEANTIME files are not included in the release.

The copied file `LICENSE.txt` is the original MEANTIME distribution licence. It identifies CC BY 4.0. `SOURCE_RECORD.md` records the byte-for-byte copy on 2026-11-07. This attribution note is not that file. The annotated MEANTIME files are not included in the release.

## Scope

The English stock-market topic is 30 documents. It is not the full 120-article
English section and not the 480-article multilingual corpus.
